title: $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes ($\ell$-adic and $\ell$-torsion $\Lambda$)
statement:
Let $\ell$ be the prime of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], invertible in $k$, and let $\Lambda$ be one of the
following commutative condensed rings ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]):

- $\underline E$ for a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$;
- $\underline{\cO}_E$ for a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, where $\cO_E$ is the ring of integers either of a
  subfield $E\subseteq\Qlb$ (with the topology restricted from $\Qlb$) or of a finite normed extension $E$ of
  $\mathbf Q_\ell$, given as its closed unit ball $\{x\in E:|x|\le1\}$;
- $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]);
- $\underline T$ for a finite discrete ring $T$ with $\ell^nT=0$ for some $n\ge0$.

Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is
bounded constructible ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $Rf_*K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]). For a general $\Lambda$ this fails: for the constant discrete ring
$\mathbf F_p$, $p$ the characteristic of $k$, and $f\colon\mathbf A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$
algebraically closed, the Artin--Schreier sequence gives $H^1(\mathbf A^1,\mathbf F_p)=k[t]/(F-1)k[t]$, which is
infinite.

external.place: This is Deligne's finiteness theorem for $Rf_*$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.1) in the pro-étale form of Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

proof.text: The setting supplies separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with $\ell$ invertible in $k$. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is Noetherian), and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. They are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], and $f$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Fix a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $P_n=A/\varpi^n$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a DVR with finite residue field. In particular $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal is principal. Since $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, clause (5) of that DVR statement writes $\ell=u\varpi^e$ with $e>0$ and $u\in A^\times$. Thus a sufficiently large power of $\ell$ kills $P_n$. Each $P_n$ is finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. When $E$ is given abstractly, as a finite normed extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ whose closed unit ball $\{x\in E:\|x\|\le1\}$ is the listed $\mathcal O_E$ (or for $\underline E$ with $E$ such a field), we first reduce to a subfield of $\Qlb$. A finite extension is algebraic, so [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] gives a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-embedding $\sigma\colon E\to\Qlb$, with image a finite subextension $E'$. The norm of $E$ is multiplicative (a normed field) and restricts to $|\cdot|_\ell$ on $\mathbf Q_\ell$ (normed algebra: $\|c\cdot1\|=|c|_\ell$); so does $x\mapsto|\sigma(x)|$, and the uniqueness in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] makes them equal. Thus $\sigma\colon E\to E'$ is an isometric ring isomorphism, a homeomorphism carrying the closed unit ball onto $\mathcal O_{E'}$. By the functoriality of $T\mapsto\underline T$ in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $\sigma$ and $\sigma^{-1}$ give mutually inverse isomorphisms of condensed rings $\underline{\mathcal O}_E\cong\underline{\mathcal O}_{E'}$ and $\underline E\cong\underline{E'}$. Their pullbacks along $p_T$ are ring-sheaf isomorphisms natural in $T$, hence compatible with the coefficient maps of every $f$; scalar transport along them is an isomorphism of module categories commuting with the pushforward and pullback of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and their derived functors, and it carries finite presentations to finite presentations, so it preserves bounded constructibility. We may therefore assume $E\subseteq\Qlb$. In either form the DVR statement applies, since its only hypothesis is an absolute value on $E$ extending $|\cdot|_\ell$. Thus $0\to A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A\to P_n\to0$ is a finite free resolution, for every $n\ge1$; this is the perfectness needed below. The coefficient identifications [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identify the pulled-back integral ring with $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$. Its inverse-image identifications are [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1), so the ordinary ringed-topos direct image for $A_T$ is the functor in the item.

Suppose first $K$ is bounded constructible over $A_X$. Its cohomology sheaves are constructible in the ring-object sense used by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: on the strata of a finite stratification they are pro-étale locally finitely presented over $A_X$, with matrix entries arbitrary sections of $A_X$. Since $X$ is Noetherian (step 1) and $A_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for the valuation topology, the implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] gives, after changing the stratification, finite constant local models $A_V\otimes_AP$ with $P$ finitely presented over $A$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. So condition (iii) applies. The characterization [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] identifies this bounded-constructible object with the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and its condition (i) supplies compatible etale-origin witnesses for the reductions. Thus $K$ is derived $\varpi$-complete, each $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_X}(P_n)_X$ has bounded constructible classical cohomology and an etale-origin representative, and all $K_n$ have cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$. This supplies completeness and the uniform reduction bounds from a theorem; they are not added to the hypotheses on $K$.

Set $M=Rf_*K$ in the ordinary, uncompleted $A_Y$-module derived category. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], $M$ is derived complete and the limit comparison identifies it with $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}K_n$. The finite-level comparison is also explicit: [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula], applied to the finite free resolution of $P_n$ from step 1, gives $M\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\simeq Rf_{*,n}K_n$, naturally in $n$. Restriction of scalars along $A_T\to(P_n)_T$ in this formula is compatible with derived direct image by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], whose $d$ identifies the two composites of restriction and direct image. Thus the right side really is the direct image in the finite coefficient category, not merely an equality after forgetting the module action.

For every $n$, choose an étale-origin representative $L_n$ of $K_n$ as furnished by step 2. The comparison [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives $Rf_{*,n}K_n\simeq\nu_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L_n$, since $f$ is qcqs and $L_n$ is bounded below. Each $P_n$ is finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] and is killed by a power of $\ell$, which is invertible on $k$. Hence [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility] applies to $L_n$ and makes this output bounded constructible. For the bound independent of $n$, use the more precise bound in [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]: applied to the integral object of step 2, it puts every $Rf_{*,n}K_n$ in $[a,b+N]$ for one $N$ depending on $f$, not $n$. Its integral direct image is the tower limit already identified with $M$ in step 3. We use no claim that $k$ itself has finite absolute cohomological dimension and no algebraic-closedness assumption.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 say exactly that $M$ is in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it is derived complete and its reductions are bounded constructible with one common interval. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] on $Y$ in the reverse direction, using its explicit clause identifying that category with condition (iii). The result is bounded cohomology with stratified finite constant local models over $A_Y$. By (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i) of [lem-sfb-integral-lfp-constant-model-comparison] ($Y$ is Noetherian) each cohomology sheaf is constructible in the ring-object sense, which is bounded constructibility as defined in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. This proves the integral case for the ambient $Rf_*$.

For $E$-coefficients, [def-sfb-rationalization-equivalence] identifies the bounded constructible $E$-category with the rationalization of the integral category, and identifies the composite with its localization functor with $E_X\otimes^L_{A_X}-$. Thus every $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ has a representative $K_0\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,A)$ with $K\simeq E_X\otimes^L_{A_X}K_0$; rationalization here is a Verdier quotient, whose objects are the original objects, not a subsequent idempotent completion. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], $E_X=A_X[1/\ell]$ is flat, and this extension is the filtered colimit of $K_0\xrightarrow{\ell}K_0\to\cdots$, a diagram with the same lower cohomological bound. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to this diagram in $A_X$-modules. It gives, in every cohomological degree, the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_m Rf_*K_0\xrightarrow{\sim} Rf_*(\varinjlim_m K_0)$, with the transition maps multiplication by $\ell$. The restriction/direct-image comparison and reflection of isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] turn this into the $E_Y$-linear isomorphism $Rf_*(E_X\otimes^L K_0)\simeq E_Y\otimes^L Rf_*K_0$. The integral case makes $Rf_*K_0$ bounded constructible, and [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-bounded-constructible] makes its extension bounded constructible. This proves the $E$ case.

For later passage to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, check the coefficient comparison for every finite $F/E$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](2), choose a finite free presentation $F_Y\simeq E_Y^{\oplus r}$. Pull this presentation back along $f^{-1}$; part (1) of the same node identifies its rings with $F_X$ and $E_X$, giving $F_X\simeq E_X^{\oplus r}$ with compatible bases. Scalar extension is exact by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat]. After restriction to $E_T$, extension sends a complex $C$ to a finite direct sum $C^{\oplus r}$. The functor $Rf_*$ is additive and triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], hence commutes with this finite sum. On every basis inclusion, the canonical coefficient-change map is the identity comparison $Rf_*C\to Rf_*C$ by the unit-counit identities. It is therefore the finite-sum isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], restriction commutes with direct image and reflects isomorphisms. Consequently $F_Y\otimes^L_{E_Y}Rf_*C\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(F_X\otimes^L_{E_X}C)$; the maps are canonical and thus compatible with $F\subset F'$.

proof.text: Now let $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. Part (3) of [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] supplies a finite $E$ and bounded constructible $C\in D(X,E)$ with $K\simeq\QbarX\otimes^L_{E_X}C$. Flatness [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat] allows the derived extension to be computed termwise. The colimit formula [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] expresses this extension as $\varinjlim_{F\supset E}(F_X\otimes_{E_X}C)$ over a small skeleton of finite subextensions. Every term has the same lower bound as $C$, by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] with fixed coefficients $E_X$ to this diagram and use the compatible comparisons from step 7. It yields $Rf_*K\simeq\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Y}\otimes^L_{E_Y}Rf_*C$, first after restriction to $E_Y$ and then in the algebraic-closure coefficient category by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. The $E$ case makes $Rf_*C$ bounded constructible. Finally [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible] says exactly that its derived extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Y}$ is bounded constructible. This proves the last coefficient case.

Finally suppose $\Lambda=\underline T$ for a finite discrete commutative ring $T$ with $\ell^nT=0$. The ring $T$ is Noetherian, being finite, and is annihilated by $\ell^n$, which is invertible in $k$ (for $n=0$, $T=0$ and every module is zero). For $Z=X,Y$ use the encoding equivalence $E_Z$ of [def-weil-pbc-common-finite-discrete-encoding] with $B=T$, from ordinary module sheaves over the constant ring $T_Z$ to module objects over $T^c_Z=p_Z^*\underline T$. It is exact, and it sends the regular module $T_Z$ to the regular module $T^c_Z$, because it transports scalars along the ring isomorphism. Put $K'=E_X^{-1}K$ termwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-constructible-local-piece], every cohomology sheaf of $K'$ is finite locally constant on the strata of a finite stratification, because its image under $E_X$ is locally finitely presented there. So $K'$ is bounded with constructible cohomology in the sense of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison]. Since $X$ is qcqs, that comparison gives $L\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},T)$ with $K'\simeq
u_X^*L$. Next, [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives $Rf_{\mathrm{proét},*}K'\simeq
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L$. By [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], applied to the finite ring $T$ and the integer $\ell^n$ invertible in $k$, $Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L$ is bounded constructible. Its cohomology sheaves have finite partitions on each member of a finite affine cover of the Noetherian scheme $Y$, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core] refines them to one finite stratification of $Y$. On each stratum the restriction is locally the constant sheaf of a finite $T$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-coefficient-direct-image-conjugation] ($f$ is qcqs by step 1, and $K'$ is bounded below), $Rf_*K$ in module objects over $T^c_Y$ is isomorphic to $E_Y(Rf_{\mathrm{proét},*}K')\simeq E_Y
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-derived-coefficient-data], $E\circ
u^*$ commutes with restriction to strata and covers. Suppose a sheaf is constant with finite value $P$ on such a piece $V$. Write $P=\operatorname{coker}(T^m	o T^n)$, which is possible since $T$ is Noetherian. Exactness of $E_V$ and $E_V(T_V)\cong T^c_V$ make its image a cokernel of a map $(T^c_V)^m	o(T^c_V)^n$, so it is finitely presented. Hence $Rf_*K$ is bounded constructible over $T^c_Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. The coefficient action is the prescribed one because [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1) identifies $f^{-1}T^c_Y$ with $T^c_X$.
